source.title: UPMC to pay DOJ nearly $1M, agrees to 10-year moratorium on gender-affirming care for trans youth

text:
Health, Science & Tech

UPMC to pay DOJ nearly $1M, agrees to 10-year moratorium on gender-affirming care for trans youth

90.5 WESA |

By

Kiley Koscinski

Published September 18, 2026 at 5:57 PM EDT

Jakob Lazzaro

/

90.5 WESA

UPMC will not resume gender-affirming care for transgender patients under the age of 19 in a new deal announced with the U.S. Department of Justice. The health system will also pay the government $950,000 to settle the Trump administration’s investigation into such care.

The health system acknowledged the agreement in a statement Friday and said it would ensure UPMC could “avoid prolonged litigation, protect patients and families from unnecessary disclosure of sensitive personal and health information, protect employees, and remain focused on patient care and advancing its core mission.”

The deal, announced Friday, comes about a month after the DOJ dropped its pursuit of the private patient records of UPMC patients that sought gender-affirming care. The formal terms of the arrangement have not been released.

“The Department of Justice is fighting to protect our nation’s children and working tirelessly to reach agreements with hospitals to end so-called ‘gender affirming care’ for minors,” said U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche.

While the health system is on the hook for nearly $1 million dollars, the deal doesn’t appear to change all that much for UPMC patients. UPMC terminated gender-affirming care for patients under 19 last summer.

The announcement is the latest move in the Trump administration’s ongoing effort to ban gender-affirming care, particularly for young people. Gender-affirming care ranges from therapy to social changes and can also include puberty blockers and hormone therapy. Such care has been shown to reduce suicide attempts and ideation among trans kids, according to a 2015 study by the Trevor Project.

The Trump administration has threatened to withhold federal funding to medical centers and prosecute doctors who provide gender-affirming care to minors, which officials have referred to as “mutilation.”

The Justice Department issued a subpoena last year seeking personal medical information about UPMC patients who received gender-affirming care as part of an investigation into what the department described as medical fraud.

A UPMC spokesperson said the agreement resolves the ongoing dispute with the DOJ.

“The agreement includes important privacy, confidentiality, and non-prosecution protections for patients, legal guardians, providers, and employees, and expressly includes no admission of wrongdoing, fault, or liability by anyone involved in providing or receiving gender-affirming care to minors at UPMC Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh or other UPMC-affiliated facilities,” the spokesperson said.

Friday’s agreement with UPMC follows similar deals struck with Mount Sinai Health System in New York, Texas Children’s Hospital, the Cleveland Clinic and Connecticut Children’s Hospital.

The DOJ simultaneously announced a similar deal Friday with New York University Langone Hospitals, which agreed to pay the government $8.5 million.

In a statement, the DOJ said UPMC “took significant steps” to cooperate with the department’s investigation “including ongoing cooperation in the department’s investigation of other entities.”

“At all times during the investigation, NYU and UPMC remained cooperative and solutions-driven,” the department said. DOJ officials did not disclose what it plans to do with the settlement money from hospitals.

UPMC’s termination of gender-affirming care services for young trans patients last July was met with fierce backlash from Pittsburgh’s LGBTQ community, local leaders and UPMC staff.

The government’s investigation into other providers remains ongoing.
